# Figure S1 | Replicate check

<!-- Generated by fig_s1_replicates.py from the campaign CSVs; do not edit by hand (re-run the script). -->

**Figure S1 | Replicate check: seeding is fast in both runs; the unseeded plateau did not replicate.**

**(a)** Best IRR found so far against simulated trials (log scale) for the two unseeded (uninformed) profitability campaigns and the two seeded (TRY-informed) ones. Solid lines are this work's campaigns: the uninformed campaign and the TRY-informed campaign seeded with 1,000 trials of the six TRY scouts (592 isobutanol-scout and 408 ethanol-scout trials: all 327 scout trials with a profitability index at least the starting strain's, plus 673 space-filling ones). Dashed lines are replicates: an uninformed campaign (run 2026-09-16) whose 50-trial space-filling start-up design, shared with seven replicate scouts, differs from this work's (51 trials, shared with the six scouts), and a TRY-informed campaign (run 2026-09-23) seeded with 1,000 trials of those seven scouts (451 isobutanol-scout, 348 ethanol-scout and 201 price-weighted-yield trials). Open circles: first trial with IRR ≥ 25 %; stars and diamonds: each campaign's best design (filled for this work, open for the replicate), every marker at its true position. The two seeded campaigns found their best designs at trials 913 and 824 (27.3 % and 27.1 %), so their stars nearly coincide: this work's filled star is drawn larger and the replicate's open star on top of it. Italic labels give the products of every best-so-far design of the two unseeded campaigns (co-producing = at least 5 g·L⁻¹ each of isobutanol and ethanol; ethanol only = less than 5 g·L⁻¹ isobutanol); the replicate's label hangs from its dashed line on a leader. The table above the axes gives, for each pair, this work / replicate. Its first two rows apply to the seeded campaigns only: the IRR of the best preloaded seed and the first simulated trial that beat it, which compares the two seeded campaigns like for like (the replicate's seeds already held a design above 25 %).

**(b)** The seven replicate scouts, drawn as in panel c of the main figure and in its family order (ethanol TRY, then isobutanol TRY; the price-weighted-yield campaign, which has no counterpart in this work, last): every completed trial (dots), the best-IRR trial visited (open marker), the design returned (filled marker; argmax of the campaign's own objective) and their connector. Marker shape gives the objective: circle yield, square titer, triangle productivity. The dashed line and the tint mark this work's uninformed plateau (15.8 %), kept as the reference although the replicate did not stay on it (a). The table gives, as in main panel c, the trials above that plateau and the share of trials losing money, and then the returned design's IRR, printed "loss" (as in the main figure and Fig. S2) for every returned design drawn in the loss band: the isobutanol titer and productivity scouts returned outright money-losers (no IRR) and the price-weighted-yield scout returned −6.0 %.

**What replicates.**

* Seeded search beat every seed within 13 and 19 trials (best seeds 22.9 % and 25.1 %; the replicate's was its isobutanol-yield scout's best visit, already above 25 %, so its 19 trials to 25 % are the same event and not a second measure of speed). This work's seeded campaign passed 25 % at trial 18. The two reached 27.3 % and 27.1 % (trials 913 and 824). After 25 trials the seeded campaigns stood at 26.2 % and 25.6 %; the unseeded ones at −11.2 % (a loss) and 9.6 %.
* The isobutanol scouts visited designs above 15.8 % (92, 2 and 5 trials for yield, titer and productivity; price-weighted yield 46), while the ethanol scouts never did (best 15.3 %).
* Every replicate scout returned a design below this work's uninformed plateau (highest: 15.5 %).
* All three campaigns that passed 27 % returned co-production designs: this work's TRY-informed 39.6 g·L⁻¹ isobutanol + 40.6 g·L⁻¹ ethanol; replicate TRY-informed 42.9 g·L⁻¹ + 11.3 g·L⁻¹; replicate uninformed 41.7 g·L⁻¹ + 29.2 g·L⁻¹.

**What does not replicate.**

* The unseeded plateau. Every improvement of this work's uninformed campaign was an ethanol-only design (all 19 best-so-far steps; first positive-IRR design at trial 53, after its 51-trial space-filling start-up design), and it stayed at 15.8 % from trial 104 to trial 2,000. The replicate's 50-trial space-filling start-up design already contained a co-production design with a positive IRR, though below the 15 % hurdle (trial 12: 9.6 % with 28.0 g·L⁻¹ isobutanol + 62.1 g·L⁻¹ ethanol), and every later improvement kept co-producing (all 21 steps): it passed 15.8 % at trial 64 (17.2 %; 11.8 g·L⁻¹ + 110.2 g·L⁻¹), 25 % at trial 104 (25.1 %; 30.7 g·L⁻¹ + 46.7 g·L⁻¹) and 27.3 % only at trial 1,603.
* In both unseeded runs every improvement kept the product class of the campaign's first positive-IRR design (in the start-up design for the replicate, trial 12; trial 53 here). With two runs this is an observation, not a test: 1 of 2 unseeded runs stayed on the ethanol-only plateau, while seeded search was fast in 2 of 2.

"Trial" is the simulated index (preloaded seeds excluded); only completed trials are used. IRRs are at default prices; a loss (IRR < 0, or no IRR for an outright money-loser) is drawn in the grey band. The replicate uninformed and scout campaigns ran before the model version was pinned; the replicate uninformed campaign's best design re-simulated to within 3 × 10⁻⁴ IRR of its recorded value.
